Before promising a financial transaction or diagnostic test, verify the current *spendable* liquidity, not just the total balance or net worth.

decisions.question: Will Trump outlive DeSantis?
decisions.thinking: Actuarially, with a 32-year age gap (Trump at 80 vs DeSantis at 47), the baseline probability of an 80-year-old outliving a 47-year-old male is roughly 5–7%, driven primarily by low baseline mortality in a 47-year-old's next 5–10 years.
decisions.uncertainty: Unanticipated severe health crises or accidents affecting DeSantis before Trump's eventual death.
decisions.resolution_risk: None identified; resolution cleanly tracks standard mortality precedence.
evidence_for: Unforeseen catastrophic health events, accidents, or acute illnesses can affect individuals regardless of age.
evidence_against: Donald Trump is 80 years old (born June 1946) while Ron DeSantis is 47 years old (born September 1978), a 32-year age gap.
US actuarial tables give an 80-year-old male an average remaining life expectancy of roughly 7–8 years, compared to over 30 years for a 47-year-old male.
The cumulative probability of a healthy 47-year-old male dying within the expected remaining lifespan of an 80-year-old is actuarially between 4% and 7%.

While Ohtani is capable of legendary power streaks, Poisson modeling and historical monthly splits put the odds of 13+ HRs in this specific 3-week window at around 5%.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether Ohtani can sustain an unprecedented ~60% HR-per-game pace across all remaining plate appearances through September 27.
decisions.resolution_risk: Criteria strictly limits home runs to the regular season ending September 27, excluding any postseason production.
evidence_for: Ohtani is an elite power hitter capable of historic multi-week home run surges, having hit 54 and 55 HRs in the prior two seasons.
Underlying contact quality remains strong with a 93.2 mph exit velocity and 15.8% barrel rate.
evidence_against: Ohtani currently has 30 home runs and needs 13 more in roughly 21 to 22 remaining regular season games.
A required pace of ~0.60 home runs per game is more than double his 2026 season pace (~0.23 HR/game) and significantly above his career peak rate.
Two-way pitching demands and potential rest days down the stretch could further limit plate appearances.
